summary: Bird Rock light (1870) in the Gulf of St. Lawrence: keepers lost to ice, a cannon blast and a 1897 storm; resident families until 1961, automated 1988, closed to visitors.

lens.note: Second-order Fresnel lens in 1870 per Lighthouse Friends; the later optic is not sourced

structures.note: Lighthouse Friends and the Îles archive give 1870; Hubert gives 1871
Tower raised onto a concrete base (Îles archive). Lighthouse Friends says height increased by 12 ft; Bourque's 1909 letter says eighteen feet (5.5 m).
31 ft per Lighthouse Friends; the archive says the wooden upper part was replaced in 1967 and later a skeletal tower replaced it
Current tower per Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights, updated 2026-07-28
New bungalow and four-room dwelling after the 1955 fire, per Lighthouse Friends

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard property; grounds and tower closed; Coast Guard crews reach the rock by helicopter. Lighthouse Friends lists five-hour excursions as offered; Les amis des phares du Saint-Laurent says they are no longer offered.

events.note: Lit 20 September 1870 per Lighthouse Friends
Construction dated 1870 by the Îles archive; Hubert dates the tower to 1871
Keeper Peter Whalen and his son carried off on the ice during a storm while sealing; both died
Gun explosion during a demonstration firing for visitors: keeper Charles Chiasson, his son and visitor Paul Chenell died
Original tower replaced by a 39-ft hexagonal wooden tower
Submarine telegraph cable taken up
Gun explosion took one of Télesphore Turbide's hands; a passing ship took him ashore after two days
Ice storm of 7 March 1897: Charles Turbide and Damien Cormier died of cold on the ice; Arsène Turbide walked to Cape Breton and died fifteen days later
Fixed white changed to occulting white, advertised 1 October 1903 (15 s shown, 5 s eclipsed); the 1905 report gives 5 s shown, 15 s eclipsed
Steamer Dominion touched bottom at Bird Rocks, 13 July 1903; 38 days in dock
Occulting clockwork broke down; light fixed white until a new machine arrived
Department announced that the explosive fog signal would be replaced by a compressed-air plant
Fog-alarm building completed and 3-inch diaphone installed (Lighthouse Friends gives 1906 for the diaphone)
Tower raised onto concrete base and reinforced
Keeper Wilfrid Bourque found dead in the water at the edge of the ice; Lighthouse Friends gives 11 March 1912
English Monarch struck Bird Rocks on 24 July 1916; continued to Sydney leaking; repaired at Montreal
Designated a sanctuary for birds by federal decree of 29 March 1919 (Îles archive); Hubert says a provincial prohibition on hunting came in 1920
Keepers poisoned by water from the rain tank in November 1922; Albin Bourque died
Fire damaged keeper's house and outbuildings on 11 July 1955 (Îles archive); Lighthouse Friends says lightning
Keepers' families no longer live on the rock; two-man teams relieved by helicopter
Upper part of tower replaced
Light automated

keepers.note: Named by Hubert as the first appointee, who refused the post; no dates given

keepers.name: J. Chapman

keepers.name: Guitté
keepers.note: Hubert: took the post after Fennelton refused, resigned in 1873 unable to adjust to the isolation; Lighthouse Friends does not name him

keepers.name: Jacques Couette
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends gives 1871. The Îles archive refers to a man named Couette offered the post about ten years before 1881; no other source confirms his tenure

keepers.name: George Preston
keepers.note: Relieved after a few months, by reason of mental infirmity (Lighthouse Friends)

keepers.name: Peter Whalen
keepers.note: Hubert calls him Patrick Whalen; Lighthouse Friends gives Peter. Died with his son on the ice, early April 1880 (Hubert gives 8 April)

keepers.name: Thomas Thivierge
keepers.note: Assistant on the 1880 seal hunt; got back to the rock next day and gave the news

keepers.name: Charles Chiasson
keepers.note: Of Havre-aux-Maisons. Appointed 25 July 1880 (Hubert) or in post from 7 July 1880 (Îles archive). Killed by the gun explosion of 23 August 1881 (Hubert, Lighthouse Friends) or 13 August 1881 (Îles archive)

keepers.name: Télesphore Turbide
keepers.note: Assistant at the time of the 1881 explosion; got the telegraph message through to Cap-aux-Meules

keepers.name: Télesphore Turbide
keepers.note: Named keeper a few weeks after the 1881 explosion; lost a hand to a gun explosion in 1891; fell badly in 1896 and resigned in September 1896

keepers.name: Arsène Turbide
keepers.note: Cousin of Télesphore Turbide (Lighthouse Friends). Walked from the ice to Baie Saint-Laurent, Cape Breton, in March 1897; died fifteen days later

keepers.name: Damien Cormier
keepers.note: Aged 60 per Hubert; died of cold on the ice in March 1897; his wife was left on the rock

keepers.name: Pierre Bourque
keepers.note: Named November 1896 (Hubert); arrived May 1897 (Lighthouse Friends), which gives his tenure from 1897 to 1905

keepers.name: Wilfrid Bourque
keepers.note: Son of Pierre Bourque. Promoted to head keeper in 1905 (Lighthouse Friends). Named as keeper at Bird Rocks in the 1907 and 1908 Marine keeper lists. Wrote a letter as keeper on 6 July 1909. Died March 1911 (Hubert) or 11 March 1912 (Lighthouse Friends) Hubert dates his death to early March 1911 (Bourque's own letter, printed by Hubert, is the source of the 1909 facts); Lighthouse Friends gives 11 March 1912.

keepers.name: Daniel Turbide
keepers.note: Assistant who held the station between Wilfrid Bourque's death and Elphège Bourque's arrival (Hubert); Lighthouse Friends gives temp. 1912

keepers.name: Elphège Bourque
keepers.note: Nephew of Wilfrid Bourque. Took the post in summer 1912 (Hubert); Lighthouse Friends gives 1912 to 1923

keepers.name: Albin Bourque
keepers.note: Brother of Elphège Bourque; took charge while Elphège was on leave; died after the November 1922 water poisoning (Hubert). Lighthouse Friends says he died on the way to Charlottetown

keepers.name: Philias Richard
keepers.note: Hubert: died about eighteen months after the 1922 poisoning. Lighthouse Friends says he died on the rock in 1922, aged 21. Conflict noted

keepers.name: Octave Langford
keepers.note: Hubert spells the name Lancford; survived the poisoning. Lighthouse Friends says he was left paralysed from the waist down

keepers.name: Antoine Éloquin
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends spelling; photo credit spells Eloquin

keepers.name: Daniel K. McLean, Jr.
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends gives '1962 – 1985?' with a question mark

keepers.name: Luke Arsenault
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends gives only c. 1980s

keepers.name: Louis Hubert
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends gives only c. 1980s

keepers.name: Philip Quinn
keepers.note: Listed by Lighthouse Friends with a question mark and no dates

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Îles archive and Lighthouse Friends give 1870 (Lighthouse Friends: first lit 20 September 1870). Hubert, writing in 1926, says the tower was erected in 1871. The record's 1870 first_lit is kept; the 1871 date is recorded as a dissent.
Hubert and Lighthouse Friends give 23 August 1881; the Îles archive gives 13 August 1881. Wikipedia (fr) gives 11 August but is not used as a source. The story gives all three.
Hubert gives early March 1911; Lighthouse Friends gives 11 March 1912.

Lighthouse Friends says a 3-inch diaphone was installed in 1906. The Marine reports show a 5-inch diaphone building under construction in the year ended 1907 and the 3-inch diaphone installed in the year ended 1908.

Hubert names Fennelton (refused), Guitté (to 1873) and Patrick Whalen (1873-1880). Lighthouse Friends names J. Chapman (1870), Jacques Couette (1871), George Preston (1872-73) and Peter Whalen (1873-80). Both lists are kept in the roster.
Hubert: named November 1896. Lighthouse Friends: arrived May 1897. The roster gives 1896 (appointment) to 1905, from Lighthouse Friends' end year.
The Îles archive gives a fire of 11 July 1955 during a Coast Guard crew's wharf repairs; Lighthouse Friends says lightning.
The 1903 advertisement says 15 s shown, 5 s eclipsed; the 1905 report says 5 s shown, 15 s eclipsed. Lighthouse Friends gives 15 s on, 5 s off. The Marine reports disagree with each other.
Bourque's 1909 letter, printed by Hubert: eleven miles from the nearest island (Brion). Lighthouse Friends: twenty-five miles northeast of the inhabited islands. The story gives both.
Bourque: about five acres. Lighthouse Friends: seven-acre summit. Both stated.
Lighthouse Friends: increased by twelve feet. Bourque's 1909 letter: eighteen feet. Both stated.

Lighthouse Friends: three-inch diaphone installed 1906. Marine reports: 1906 says the explosive signal would be replaced; 1907 lists a 3-inch diaphone supplied and $7,100; 1908 says it was installed. Bourque dates a compressed-air whistle to 1907. The story gives these.
Marine 1903-1905 reports: occulting from 1903 (15 s on, 5 s eclipsed), then 5 s on and 15 s eclipsed in 1905. Bourque's letter says the light became revolving in 1904. The story gives all three.
Lighthouse Friends: a government vessel cut through the ice and rescued Cormier's wife. Hubert (Bourque's letter): five seal hunters arrived on 9 March. The story gives both.

Hubert (Bourque's letter): early March 1911. Lighthouse Friends: 11 March 1912. Both stated. The Marine keeper list for 1911-12 (fiscal, printed p. 65) reads Bird Rocks 'Vacant' in the OCR; not checked on the page image and not used.
Îles archive: federal decree 29 March 1919. Lighthouse Friends: 1919. Hubert: provincial government reserved the rock and banned hunting in 1920. All three stated.
Lighthouse Friends lists five-hour excursions as offered; Les amis des phares du Saint-Laurent says they are no longer offered. Both stated; the later source is preferred for the present tense.
Îles archive gives the date and the Coast Guard wharf repair, not the cause. Lighthouse Friends gives lightning. Stated as Lighthouse Friends' account.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27 (147 quotes found on the first run). Re-attributed Hubert's paragraphs that are Bourque's 1909 letter as printed by Hubert. Checked the Marine keeper-list rows on the page image: 1907 printed p. 138 (Bourque, Wilfrid - Bird Rocks, Nov. 15, 1905) and 1908 printed p. 183 (Bird Rocks - W. Bourque). Fiscal-year label on the 1917 casualty footnote corrected to fiscal 1916-17 (year ended 31 March 1917). Removed 'Before the light, the birds had the place to themselves' (not sourced as stated), 'boat_only' (not sourced; helicopter access is sourced). 'Count' changed to 'estimate' for the 1909 area; 'widow' changed to 'wife' for Cormier's wife. Lighthouse Friends' distance (25 miles), height increase (12 ft) and rescue account are stated alongside the Bourque/Hubert figures. Sources disagree on the first keepers, the explosion date (13, 23 Aug 1881; French Wikipedia gives 11 Aug but is not cited), the Wilfrid Bourque death year (1911 Hubert vs 1912 LF), the first lighting year (1870 vs Hubert's 1871), the diaphone year (LF 1906 vs Marine reports 1907-08), the cause of the 1955 fire, and the 1919/1920 sanctuary dates. French Wikipedia says the light was extinguished in 2011; the Coast Guard list (modified 2026-07-28) still gives a year-round light, so the current status needs a human check. Keeper roster lines taken from Lighthouse Friends are its published list and have not been checked against Marine keeper tables beyond Wilfrid Bourque (1907, 1908). Hubert's 1926 letter quotation is Wilfrid Bourque's own 1909 letter. The 1939 Roosevelt visit rests on Lighthouse Friends' summary of a 1971 newspaper interview, which was not read; treat it as unverified. Hubert's 1926 book is public domain on Wikisource. The Marine annual report cited as 1903 covers the fiscal year ended 30 June 1903 and gives an account of events after that date, so the 1 Oct 1903 change and the 13 July 1903 grounding are in its post-year account. Five acres (Bourque) vs seven acres (LF) for the summit.
